classification.difficultyReason: Parts a, b and d are direct recognitions: split a marked right angle, a straight angle, or a straight-line pair. Part c is the hardest essential demand. The student must use the 35° label to get EBF = 55°, deduce ABF = 90° from the straight line and the right angle, add the two angles, and then classify 145° as neither complementary nor supplementary. That is a short linked chain with a diagram read and a 'neither' interpretation, so it is harder than the one-step angle facts in p72-q2 and p72-q3. It is easier than p18-q8, which needs reasoning about insufficient information. It is also just easier than p73-q6, which adds algebraic angle expressions. The solution implies where the 35° and the right-angle mark sit, but the diagram spec is not supplied, so the placement relies on that reading.

content.prompt: State whether these pairs of angles are complementary, supplementary, or neither.

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\angle CBE+\angle EBF&=\angle CBF\\&=90^\circ\end{align*}$$They split the marked right angle $CBF$, so they are complementary.
$$\begin{align*}\angle ABE+\angle CBE&=\angle ABC\\&=180^\circ\end{align*}$$They form the straight angle $ABC$, so they are supplementary.

$$\begin{align*}\angle EBF&=90^\circ-35^\circ=55^\circ\\\angle ABF&=180^\circ-90^\circ=90^\circ\\\angle ABF+\angle EBF&=90^\circ+55^\circ=145^\circ\end{align*}$$The sum is not $90^\circ$ or $180^\circ$, so they are neither.
$$\begin{align*}\angle ABF+\angle FBC&=\angle ABC\\&=180^\circ\end{align*}$$They form the straight angle $ABC$, so they are supplementary.
